methods.label: Cancel consecutive numerator and denominator factors
methods.explanation:
For the consecutive product, \(n\) is an integer with \(n\ge3\). Rewrite each factor as
\[
1-\frac1k=\frac{k-1}{k}.
\]
The product becomes
\[
\frac23\cdot\frac34\cdot\frac45\cdots\frac{n-1}{n}.
\]
Every integer from \(3\) through \(n-1\) occurs once in a numerator and once in a denominator, so these nonzero factors cancel. Only the first numerator, \(2\), and the last denominator, \(n\), remain. Thus the product is \(\boxed{\frac2n}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). For \(n=3\), the single factor is already \(2/3\), agreeing with the formula.
methods.levelReason: Rewriting fractions and canceling common factors give a complete elementary solution.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central target is exposing cancellation in a finite product and retaining the correct endpoints, exactly the scope of math:telescoping. Rational arithmetic supports rewriting the factors. Neither factorial notation nor induction is needed.
